description.p: KEMU is a traditional, direct-to-QEMU desktop frontend for Linux, built with Qt 6 Widgets and KDE Frameworks 6 for desktop integration. It provides a simple and intuitive graphical interface to manage local virtual machines.

ul.li: Create, edit, and delete QEMU virtual machines
Integrated D-Bus viewer with audio and clipboard sharing
Support for GTK and SDL display backends
Hot-swapping of ISO and floppy images
User-mode networking via passt or built-in SLIRP, plus rootless virtual networks within Linux user namespaces
Portable VM storage: VMs are stored as self-contained directories with relative start scripts
Export and import VMs as compressed archives (.kemu.tar.zst) for seamless backup or migration
OVA export and import for cross-platform interoperability

description.p: Split VM creation into compact and editor dialogs, parallel capability probing, and GPU cursor performance optimizations.
Flatpak sandbox support, SLIRP networking fallback, viewer media controls, and improved OVA imports.
Introduced integrated D-Bus viewer, QMP live snapshots, and power-off save-state support.
Floppy disk image support, MS-DOS/FreeDOS templates, ISA-PC chipset constraints, and new network devices.
Initial release featuring basic VM management and UI.
